issues.failure_explanation: The first relation of the lemma, sum_q a_{pq} psi_q = w_p, is false for N >= 2. The proof's final step asserts sum_q [kappa^{-1}]_{pq} w_q psi_q = w_p, which does not follow from the established identity sum_q [kappa^{-1}]_{pq} psi_q = 1 (the factor w_q inside the sum cannot be removed), and the displayed equivalence 'sum_q a_{pq} psi_q = w_p iff sum_q [kappa^{-1}]_{pq} psi_q = 1' is invalid. Exact computation for N = 2 gives (kappa w)_0 = (45+29 sqrt(15))/324 ≈ 0.4855 whereas (w∘psi)_0 = w_0 psi_0 = (75+15 sqrt(15))/324 ≈ 0.4108; since sum_q a_{pq} psi_q = w_p would require kappa w = w∘psi, the relation fails. The true analogous identity is the one the paper actually uses, sum_p a_{pq} psitilde_p = w_q (with w_q factored out of the sum), which is proved correctly; the false relation is not used downstream.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the false relation sum_q a_{pq} psi_q = w_p and its invalid proof from Lemma ader_int_prop; the remaining relations are true and suffice for all downstream uses (in particular sum_p a_{pq} psitilde_p = w_q used in eq:ader_dg_node_sol_by_q).
issues.overall_effect: One identity in Lemma ader_int_prop is false for N >= 2; it is advertised in a remark as useful for software testing and assertions, so it could mislead implementation checks. No labelled formal result relies on this identity, so no theorem is invalidated.
issues.title: False identity sum_q a_{pq} psi_q = w_p in Lemma ader_int_prop
issues.why_classification: The false identity is unused downstream; removing it is a short local edit that preserves every substantive claim, and the true identity on which the paper actually relies is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In cases $N = 1$, $2$, $3$, the Butcher tables take the form:
The $r = 0$ in $C(N)$ corresponds to the relation: $\sum_{q = 0}^{N} a_{pq} = \tau_{p}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed N=1 tableau has wrong off-diagonal entries. From a = kappa^{-1} mu with the one-panel Legendre-Gauss nodes tau_{0,1} = 1/2 ∓ sqrt(3)/6 and weights w_{0,1} = 1/2 one obtains a = [[1/3, -(sqrt(3)-1)/6], [(1+sqrt(3))/6, 1/3]], i.e. a_{12} = -(sqrt(3)-1)/6 ≈ -0.1220 and a_{21} = (1+sqrt(3))/6 ≈ 0.4553, whereas the table displays a_{12} = -(1-sqrt(3))/2 = (sqrt(3)-1)/2 ≈ 0.3660 and a_{21} = (1-sqrt(3))/2 ≈ -0.3660. The displayed matrix violates the paper's own C(1) condition sum_q a_{pq} = tau_p: its row sums are 1/3+(sqrt(3)-1)/2 = (3 sqrt(3)-1)/6 ≈ 0.6994 and 1/3-(sqrt(3)-1)/2 = (3-3 sqrt(3))/6 ≈ -0.0327, not tau_1 = (3-sqrt(3))/6 and tau_2 = (3+sqrt(3))/6. The N=2 and N=3 tables are consistent with a = kappa^{-1} mu (the N=2 table satisfies C(2), D(1), D(2) and kappa a = mu), so the error is isolated to the N=1 display.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the N=1 A-matrix with the correct [[1/3, -(sqrt(3)-1)/6], [(1+sqrt(3))/6, 1/3]], a routine computation from a = kappa^{-1} mu; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: A reader implementing the N=1 method from the displayed tableau obtains a wrong RK matrix that fails even the C(1) row-sum condition. The abstract definition a = kappa^{-1} mu, the N=2 and N=3 tables, and all theorems and stability results are unaffected.
issues.title: Incorrect N=1 Butcher tableau (off-diagonal entries of a)
issues.why_classification: The error is isolated to an illustrative display; the correct coefficients follow by a short routine computation, and no theorem, guarantee, or downstream result depends on the displayed N=1 entries.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The nodes $\{\tau_{p}\}_{p = 0}^{N}$ and weights $\{w_{p}\}_{p = 0}^{N}$ of the quadrature formula (\ref{eq:gl_rule}) ensure (see Lemma~3.3.1 in book~\cite{Dekker_Verwer_1984}) that $B(2N+2)$ is satisfied. Lemmas~\ref{lemma:cn_cond} and~\ref{lemma:dn_cond} prove the satisfaction of $C(N)$ and $D(N)$, respectively.
the simplifying condition $C(N+1)$ is not satisfied

issues.failure_explanation: The proof invokes 'Butcher's theorem' for the implication B(2N+2) ∧ C(N) ∧ D(N) ⇒ p_RK = 2N+1. In its standard form (Butcher; Dekker-Verwer, Thm. 3.4) the simplifying-conditions theorem states that B(2η) ∧ C(η) ∧ D(ζ) yields p ≥ min(2η, η+ζ+1); applied with the method's indices (η = N, ζ = N, using B(2N) ⊆ B(2N+2)) it gives only p ≥ 2N, not 2N+1. The order-(2N+1) conditions include the chain condition sum_b a^{2N} = 1/(2N+1)!, which is not implied by the simplifying conditions alone (the paper itself notes C(N+1) fails). The method does in fact have order 2N+1 — the nonlinear order conditions follow from B(2N+2), C(N), D(N) with b = w, and the chain conditions from the Pade property of R(z) proved later in Theorem pade_approx — so the conclusion is true, but the cited theorem does not establish it as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the order directly: verify the nonlinear order conditions up to 2N+1 from B(2N+2), C(N), D(N) (using b = w), and the chain (linear) conditions from the Pade property of R(z) established in Theorem pade_approx; a contained argument with no loss of the result.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the paper's central advertised order (p_RK = 2N+1, superconvergence at the nodes) is unsupported as written: the cited simplifying-conditions theorem yields only p ≥ 2N for the stated hypotheses. The conclusion is true, so Corollary coroll:order_ader_dg_nodes, the abstract/conclusion claims, and the empirical reference orders survive; only the justification of Theorem order_rk needs repair.
issues.title: Order theorem proved via a misapplied simplifying-conditions theorem
issues.why_classification: The advertised order 2N+1 is true and fully survives, but the proof as written relies on a theorem implication stronger than the cited theorem provides; repairing it needs a contained but nontrivial order-conditions argument rather than a local fix, while causing no loss of the result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The local solution $\mathbf{q}_{n}$ is the Lagrange interpolation polynomial of degree $N$ (\ref{eq:local_sol}) whose coefficients $\{\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{p}\}_{p = 0}^{N}$ are the solution of the system of equations (\ref{eq:snae_lstdg}), where $\mathbf{u}_{n}$ is known with the approximation order $p_{\rm RK} = 2N+1$.
The error estimate for the Lagrange interpolation polynomial can be presented in the form:

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds |q_n(t) - utilde(t)| by the degree-N Lagrange interpolation error Δt^{N+1}/(N+1)! max|utilde^{(N+1)}|, but this bound applies only to the interpolant of utilde at the N+1 nodes, whereas q_n interpolates the numerical stage values qhat_{n,p}. The stage values differ from the exact values: |qhat_{n,p} - utilde(tau_p)| = O(Δt_n^{N+1}) (stage order N, following from C(N)). The displayed estimate therefore does not apply as written, and the proof omits this necessary contribution. The conclusion (local order N+1) is correct once the stage error is included via the triangle inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the stage-error estimate max_p |qhat_{n,p} - utilde(tau_p)| = O(Δt_n^{N+1}) (which follows from the simplifying condition C(N)) to the interpolation error via the triangle inequality; a one-line repair with no change of conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma local_sol_order_L_inf (local solution has order N+1) is incomplete: the interpolation bound is applied to the numerical interpolant as if it reproduced the exact solution at the nodes. The conclusion is correct, so Theorem local_sol_order_L_inf and Theorem local_sol_order_L_p, which build on it, survive.
issues.title: Local-solution order lemma proved with an inapplicable interpolation bound
issues.why_classification: The conclusion (local order N+1) is correct and the repair is a standard one-line stage-error addition from C(N); all downstream local-solution theorems survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix $a = \kappa^{-1}\cdot\mu$ in the denominator is invertible and $\mathrm{rank}(a) = N+1$.

Therefore $\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{I} - \boldsymbol{\psi}\mathbf{1}^{T}) = N$, and $\mathrm{rank}(a - \mathbf{1}\mathbf{w}^{T}) = N$. Therefore the numerator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $P_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N-1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof correctly computes rank(a) = N+1 and rank(a - 1 w^T) = N, but then misstates the resulting degrees of R(z) = det(I-za+z 1 w^T)/det(I-za): the denominator det(I-za) has degree N+1 (not N, as claimed) because rank(a) = N+1, and the numerator det(I-z(a-1 w^T)) has degree N (not N-1, as claimed) because rank(a-1 w^T) = N. With the corrected degrees (numerator N, denominator N+1) and the method's order 2N+1, the conclusion that R(z) is the (N,N+1)-Pade approximant of exp(z) follows by Pade uniqueness, so the theorem's statement is true.

failure_location.quote: The denominator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the two degree statements to numerator degree N and denominator degree N+1, as forced by the paper's own rank computations; the conclusion then follows immediately by Pade uniqueness.
issues.overall_effect: Two intermediate degree claims in the proof of the Pade theorem are wrong (off by one), but the conclusion — R(z) is the (N,N+1)-Pade approximant — is correct, and the L-stability theorem and the alternative A-stability corollary, which use R(infinity) = 0, are unaffected.
issues.title: Pade theorem proof misstates the numerator and denominator degrees
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is correct and the two misstatements are forced corrections from the paper's own rank computations; no dependent result or guarantee is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the residual term of the $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ is $\exp(z) - R_{N, N+1}(z) = O(z^{2N+2})$, so the approximation order of the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method $p_{\rm RK} = 2N+1$

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary infers the method's order p_RK = 2N+1 from the residual estimate exp(z) - R_{N,N+1}(z) = O(z^{2N+2}) of the stability function. This inference is invalid: for Runge-Kutta methods the order of the stability function R(z) is only an upper bound for the method's order (distinct RK methods can share the same stability function yet have different orders), so the Pade residual alone cannot establish p_RK = 2N+1. The conclusion is nevertheless true — it is the content of Theorem order_rk — so only the 'alternative proof' claim is defective.

failure_location.quote: By Theorem~3.11 in~\cite{Hairer_book_2}, the residual term of the $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ is $\exp(z) - R_{N, N+1}(z) = O(z^{2N+2})$, so the approximation order of the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method $p_{\rm RK} = 2N+1$, which is an alternative proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:order_rk}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the 'alternative proof' claim (or replace it with a correct argument combining the Pade property with the simplifying conditions); the corollary's statement needs no change.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's claim of an independent 'alternative proof' of the order is invalid; the conclusion p_RK = 2N+1 is already established by Theorem order_rk, so no other result is affected.
issues.title: Invalid 'alternative proof' of the order from the Pade residual
issues.why_classification: Only the 'alternative proof' framing is defective; the corollary's conclusion is already proven elsewhere, so a one-sentence deletion repairs it with no mathematical loss.
